page: Microsoft Azure E80ids_v4 is an isolated, memory-optimized virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at a base frequency of 2.6 GHz. It provides 80 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 40 physical cores with two threads per core. Memory allocation is 504.0 GB of RAM, equating to 6.3 GB per core, supported by 35 MB of L3 cache. In addition to standard remote storage capabilities, it incorporates 2577 GB of direct-attached local SSD storage. The platform contains no hardware accelerators or GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate significant compute and memory parallelism alongside high throughput. In multi-threaded evaluations, the instance achieved strong ratings, including 74299.35 in stress-ng multi-core and 53855.93 in PassMark CPU tests. Memory subsystems recorded 214.64 GB/sec in uncached 256 MB reads and 4152.66 GB/sec in cached reads, scoring in the top 25 percent for PassMark memory. Data processing benchmarks reflect strong operational capacity, logging 22751.33 in PassMark database operations and 64.91 million operations per second on Redis SET tests. Conversely, single-threaded metrics such as single-core stress-ng (1477.68) and Geekbench single-core (1361.0) remain within median tiers, while LLM generative inference performs poorly due to the lack of dedicated tensor accelerators.

The hardware configuration provides high resource density for workloads requiring vast RAM pools alongside fast local scratch space. It is well suited for large relational databases, in-memory caches, big data analytics engines, and enterprise compilation pipelines, though organizations prioritizing single-thread latency or real-time deep learning inference should seek alternate architectural profiles.
description: Microsoft Azure E80ids_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz. It provides 80 dedicated vCPUs across 40 physical cores, 504.0 GB of RAM (6.3 GB per core), and 2577 GB of direct-attached local SSD storage. Hyper-threading and hardware vector extensions like AVX-512 are present, while dedicated GPUs are omitted. In synthetic benchmarks, the server excels across multi-threaded and memory-intensive workflows, registering strong results in PassMark database operations, Redis SET throughput (64.91 million operations per second), and multi-threaded compression. In contrast, single-threaded processing and LLM text generation metrics reflect architectural constraints typical of CPU-only platforms. The instance is suitable for large-scale relational databases, in-memory key-value caching, software compilation, and enterprise analytics pipelines that demand extensive RAM capacity and high sustained multi-core performance.
